# Project Bioengineering

## 27200 Project: Macrophage Response to IFNg and Salmonella

# 1. Load Libraries

First, we load all the R packages needed for our analysis.

```{r}
# Uncomment and run once if packages are missing:
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "ggplot2", "pheatmap", "ggrepel", "msigdbr", "igraph"))
# BiocManager::install(c("SummarizedExperiment", "DESeq2", "fgsea", "STRINGdb"))

library(tidyverse)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(DESeq2)
library(ggplot2)
library(pheatmap)
library(ggrepel)
library(fgsea)
library(msigdbr)
library(STRINGdb)
library(igraph)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2. Load Data & Metadata

We load the gene expression object and the sample information table (metadata.tsv), making sure the sample names match in the exact same order.

```{r}
# folder path
base_dir <- "~/Documents/27200/macrophage_subset12_salmon"

# load the gene expression data (SummarizedExperiment)
se <- readRDS(file.path(base_dir, "salmon.merged.gene.SummarizedExperiment.rds"))

# load the sample metadata
meta_path <- file.path(base_dir, "pipeline_info/sample_metadata_macrophage_subset12.tsv")
meta <- read.delim(meta_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# align metadata rows with count matrix columns
rownames(meta) <- meta$sample
meta <- meta[colnames(se), ]
stopifnot(identical(colnames(se), rownames(meta))) # Must be TRUE

# attach metadata to the object and clean Ensembl IDs (remove version numbers like .18)
colData(se) <- DataFrame(meta)
rownames(se) <- sub("\\..*", "", rownames(se))

# check experimental design (supposed to be 48 samples = 12*4)
table(colData(se)$line, colData(se)$condition)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 3. Quality Control & Sanity Checks

Before running statistics, we prepare the DESeq2 dataset (\~ line + condition to account for donor differences), verify sample sex using Y-chromosome genes, check macrophage markers, and remove lowly expressed genes.

```{r}
# set factor levels ("naive" is our control)
colData(se)$condition <- factor(colData(se)$condition, 
                                levels = c("naive", "IFNg", "SL1344", "IFNg_SL1344"))
colData(se)$line <- factor(colData(se)$line)
colData(se)$sex  <- factor(colData(se)$sex)

# round counts to integers (required by DESeq2)
counts_rounded <- round(assay(se, "counts"))

# DESeq2 object
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = counts_rounded,
  colData   = colData(se),
  design    = ~ line + condition
)
rowData(dds)$gene_name <- rowData(se)$gene_name
```

Sanity Check 1:

```{r}
# verify donor sex using Y-chromosome genes (XIST is silenced in iPSCs)
y_genes <- c("UTY", "DDX3Y", "RPS4Y1", "KDM5D")
y_counts <- counts(dds)[rowData(dds)$gene_name %in% y_genes, ]

sex_check <- data.frame(
  sample       = colnames(dds),
  line         = colData(dds)$line,
  sex_metadata = colData(dds)$sex,
  Y_gene_sum   = colSums(y_counts)
)
head(sex_check, 10)
```

↑ there are some alignment errors but it's normal\
you can clearly see that there are way more Ygenes in males

Sanity Check 2:

```{r}
# check macrophage lineage markers
mac_genes <- c("CD14", "FCGR3A", "MRC1")
mac_counts <- counts(dds)[rowData(dds)$gene_name %in% mac_genes, ]
rownames(mac_counts) <- rowData(dds)$gene_name[rowData(dds)$gene_name %in% mac_genes]
summary(t(mac_counts))
```

↑ all the mins are over 1000 meaning that the macrophage were correctly differenciated

```{r}
#nrow(dds)
cat("Genes kept before filtering:", nrow(dds), "\n")

# pre-filtering: Keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 12 samples
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= 12
dds <- dds[keep, ]

cat("Genes kept after filtering:", nrow(dds), "\n")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 4. Exploratory Data Visualization (PCA)

We apply Variance-Stabilizing Transformation (vst) so highly expressed genes do not dominate the plot, and visualize how samples group together in a Principal Component Analysis (PCA).

```{r}
# transform counts with vst
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = TRUE)

pcaData <- plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = c("condition", "line", "sex"), returnData = TRUE)
percentVar <- round(100 * attr(pcaData, "percentVar"))

ggplot(pcaData, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = condition, shape = sex)) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA of Human iPSC-Derived Macrophages",
    x     = paste0("PC1: ", percentVar[1], "% variance"),
    y     = paste0("PC2: ", percentVar[2], "% variance"),
    color = "Condition",
    shape = "Donor Sex"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

↑ you can clearly see that the conditions are clearly separated and have a clean distribution with the donor sex

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 5. Differential Expression Analysis (DESeq2)

### Pairwise Comparisons (`~ line + condition`)

We test which genes change significantly (padj \< 0.05 and \|log2FoldChange\| \> 1) between treatments.

```{r}
# run DESeq2
dds <- DESeq(dds)

# extract results between out conditions
res_IFNg   <- results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "IFNg", "naive"), alpha = 0.05)
res_Salm   <- results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "SL1344", "naive"), alpha = 0.05)
res_Both   <- results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "IFNg_SL1344", "naive"), alpha = 0.05)
res_Primed <- results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "IFNg_SL1344", "SL1344"), alpha = 0.05)

# summary table of signiticant genes
deg_summary <- data.frame(
  Comparison = c("IFNg vs naive", "SL1344 vs naive", "IFNg_SL1344 vs naive", "IFNg_SL1344 vs SL1344 (Priming)"),
  Up_regulated = c(
    sum(res_IFNg$padj < 0.05 & res_IFNg$log2FoldChange > 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(res_Salm$padj < 0.05 & res_Salm$log2FoldChange > 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(res_Both$padj < 0.05 & res_Both$log2FoldChange > 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(res_Primed$padj < 0.05 & res_Primed$log2FoldChange > 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  Down_regulated = c(
    sum(res_IFNg$padj < 0.05 & res_IFNg$log2FoldChange < -1, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(res_Salm$padj < 0.05 & res_Salm$log2FoldChange < -1, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(res_Both$padj < 0.05 & res_Both$log2FoldChange < -1, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(res_Primed$padj < 0.05 & res_Primed$log2FoldChange < -1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)
deg_summary$Total <- deg_summary$Up_regulated + deg_summary$Down_regulated
deg_summary
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Synergy Iteraction Model (\~ line + IFNg + Salmonella + IFNg : Salmonella)

we are trying to test if the IFNg + Salmonella equals just a summed effect or if there is actually an interaction between them that can change something in gene expression (synergy or saturation)

```{r}
# set factor levels for IFNg and Salmonella, no is reference
colData(dds)$IFNg <- factor(colData(dds)$IFNg, levels = c("no", "yes"))
colData(dds)$Salmonella <- factor(colData(dds)$Salmonella, levels = c("no", "yes"))

dds_int <- dds

design(dds_int) <- ~ line + IFNg + Salmonella + IFNg:Salmonella
dds_int <- DESeq(dds_int)

res_interaction <- results(dds_int, name = "IFNgyes.Salmonellayes", alpha = 0.05)

# create a clean dataset with gene names
interaction_df <- as.data.frame(res_interaction)
interaction_df$gene_name <- rowData(dds_int)$gene_name
interaction_df <- interaction_df %>% 
  filter(!is.na(padj)) %>%
  arrange(padj)

# top 10 interaction genes
head(interaction_df[, c("gene_name", "baseMean", "log2FoldChange", "padj")], 10)

pos_synergy <- interaction_df %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange > 1)

cat("Positively synergistic genes:", nrow(pos_synergy), "\n")
```

↑ these are the top 10 genes that have a logfoldchange difference between priming with salmonella and no priming
